record.paper_title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and open problems related to filamentation
record.original_question:
For the modified focusing cubic NLS

 i P_2(epsilon nabla) partial_t v + Delta v + |v|^2 v = 0,

assume that the positive self-adjoint operator P_2(epsilon nabla) gives only partial off-axis regularization, meaning it controls derivatives only in some distinguished directions rather than the full H^1 norm. Can one develop both the local and the global well-posedness theory in that partial off-axis case, and in particular decide whether this partial off-axis dependence is enough to prevent finite-time breakdown of solutions that would blow up for the standard focusing cubic NLS?

evidence.quote: (60) iP2(ε∇)∂tv + ∆v + |v|^2v = 0, where d = 2 in the case of no GVD, and d = 3 in the case of anomalous GVD.

(66) (P2(ε∇)v, v) & ||v||^2_{L^2} + ε^2 Σ_{k=1}^j ||v_k · ∇v||^2_{L^2}, for vectors v_k in R^d, k = 1, . . . , j, where j = 1 if d = 2, and j = 1 or j = 2 if d = 3 so that the right-hand side of (66) does not control the full H^1 norm.
Now, it would be interesting to investigate whether a suitable well-posedness theory together with the conserved quantities given by the energy and (61) yield global existence.

Open Problem 4. Investigate both the local and global well-posedness for equation (60) in the case of partial off-axis dependence. In particular, does the modification of the focusing cubic NLS (1) by the addition of a partial off-axis dependence prevent the finite-time breakdown of the solutions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the modified focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
  i P_2(ε∇) ∂_t v + Δ v + |v|^2 v = 0,    (t,x) ∈ ℝ × ℝ^d,
where d ∈ {2,3}, ε > 0 is a fixed parameter, and P_2(ε∇) is a positive self-adjoint Fourier multiplier of order two with symbol P_2(εξ) ≥ 0. Assume that P_2 provides only a "partial off-axis" regularization in the sense that there exist unit vectors v_1,…,v_j ∈ ℝ^d (with j = 1 if d = 2, and j ∈ {1,2} if d = 3) and a constant C > 0 such that for every Schwartz function v,
  (P_2(ε∇) v, v)_{L^2} ≥ C ( ‖v‖_{L^2}^2 + ε^2 Σ_{k=1}^{j} ‖v_k · ∇ v‖_{L^2}^2 ),
while the right-hand side does not control the full H^1 norm of v (so derivatives in directions orthogonal to span{v_1,…,v_j} are not controlled by the quadratic form of P_2).

The equation formally conserves the L^2-type quantity (P_2(ε∇) v, v)_{L^2} and the standard energy E(v) = ½‖∇v‖_{L^2}^2 − ¼‖v‖_{L^4}^4.

(a) Develop a local well-posedness theory for the Cauchy problem associated with this equation in a function space adapted to the partial off-axis regularization.

(b) Develop a global well-posedness theory in the same setting.

(c) Decide whether the partial off-axis dependence encoded by P_2(ε∇) is sufficient to prevent the finite-time blow-up phenomena that occur for the standard focusing cubic NLS i ∂_t u + Δ u + |u|^2 u = 0 in dimensions d = 2, 3.
artifact.status_search_result: Antonelli, Arbunich, and Sparber, "Regularizing Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations Through Partial Off-axis Variations" (SIAM J. Math. Anal. 51 (2019), 110–130), establish local and global well-posedness for this class of NLS equations with only partial off-axis regularization, including in L^2-supercritical regimes, and show that the partial off-axis term is sufficient to prevent finite-time blow-up. This is explicitly framed as resolving the stated open problem.

status_evidence.title: Regularizing Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations Through Partial Off-axis Variations
status_evidence.snippet: Global well-posedness in L^2-supercritical situations, even in the case of only partial off-axis dependence, providing an answer to an open problem posed by Dumas, Lannes, and Szeftel.
status_evidence.claim: The local and global well-posedness questions and the prevention of finite-time blow-up are resolved affirmatively in the partial off-axis case.

status_evidence.title: Regularizing Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations Through Partial Off-axis Variations (Semantic Scholar)
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the initial value problem for such models and obtains global well-posedness, even in the case of only partial off-axis dependence.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the affirmative resolution of the open problem by Antonelli–Arbunich–Sparber.
